agent_priors_used: General prior, not SPIDER evidence: locally rational continuation is a documented failure mode; a lane left on its own next_question drifts toward incremental refinements of a spent thread.

General prior, not SPIDER evidence: if comparators sit at ceiling, no treatment effect is identifiable regardless of sample size, so a non-degeneracy/dynamic-range check must precede any benchmark spend.

General prior, not SPIDER evidence: end-to-end agent cost is dominated by exploration, verification and repair rather than by stored-representation size, which favors counter-based work-avoided metrics.

General prior, not SPIDER evidence: memory/cache invalidation is harder than population and un-questioned stale knowledge is a correctness hazard, so false-accept-first freshness/repair metrics matter more than coverage.
General prior, not SPIDER evidence: a prerequisite observed failing identically across lanes should be repaired once, not rediscovered per lane - but only if it is reachable by an authorized writer.

General prior, not SPIDER evidence: serial gating chains make off-path breadth cheap but not free; off-path lanes should be parked or pointed at the highest-value non-gated question rather than kept busy.

allocation.comparative_reasoning: LEGACY: DISTINCT_EXTENSION. The legacy brief's P2-MIND2WEB (retrieval 47/176 = 26.7%; archived Codex section 1) and P2-WP002B (no website-holdout result) bound reachability/transfer generally but do not measure discovery-channel reachability or acquisition cost versus hop depth. The legacy index does contain Intel discovery artifacts (results/intel/reproductions/cycle5/discovery_checks.json sha 64a77a94cfbc413613815414a5070ad80357de8e; cycle6 discovery manifests e.g. sha fd7ee084842379617aa70ee0ac1786c0a5aee500), but these are reproduction/route captures, not a site-native-discovery reachability or hop-cost scaling measurement; exact sources were not re-audited (search limitation declared). I reject the Scout's alternative orthogonal probes on duplication grounds: structured intent canonicalization duplicates C-SEMANTIC-RESOLVE, incremental/delta propagation duplicates the C-DELTA-REPAIR work assigned to Graph, and compile-then-replay duplicates SPIDER's own core and the withdrawn replay claim. This is not a pointless rerun: v1 never took a measurement (empty frame), and the v2 redesign adds the pre-freeze attainability certificate that makes the question falsifiable in both directions.
allocation.question: On the credential-free GET-only stdlib-HTTP substrate, over a frozen multi-host pool confirmed during DESIGN by a pre-freeze attainability certificate to contain DEEP (hop>=3) state-carrying items on at least two distinct hosts/engines, does site-native discovery (robots.txt/sitemap, on-site search, RSS/Atom, JSON-LD enumeration) let a fresh agent reach those DEEP items in O(1) GETs (K<=3: one discovery GET plus the item-page GET plus one spare), and is the unconditional cost of obtaining one fresh valid instance of a state item flat or growing in the item's shortest-path hop distance - deciding whether persistent cross-episode state can buy a work reduction that grows with Web depth, or whether fresh-instance acquisition is a constant-cost procedure and effort should move to procedure caching and substrate expansion?
allocation.rationale: Frontier's active pre-freeze mandate pivots to a C-SEMANTIC-RESOLVE micro-benchmark, but that claim has now lost three consecutive packets to the same shared control-plane defect (unsatisfiable freeze-time code binding) and the cumulative program audit judged it not worth reopening as an isolated micro-benchmark; more importantly, semantic resolution is inside SPIDER's current basin and belongs to Product/Graph, whereas Frontier's charter is to leave the basin. The genuinely orthogonal, architecture-changing question - left entirely unmeasured when the prior v1 site-native-discovery packet froze an empty sampling frame (0 seeds, 0 DEEP, 0 hosts) - is whether deep acquisition is path-bound or O(1)-discoverable. Either direction changes an important decision: a flat cost says stop treating fresh-instance acquisition as an optimization target and move to procedure caching/substrate expansion; a growing cost gives path/procedure persistence a measurable amortization surface. The v2 design uses the six-check design-contract v2 plus design_review.json and a pre-freeze attainability certificate, so it fails loudly and cheaply if the DEEP pool is not constructible instead of freezing another empty frame.

director_mandate.portfolio_assessment: Effective claim state is unchanged from the last sync and all six lanes are live with active PREFREEZE experiments; no frozen experiment is awaiting completion. The program's one decisive deliverable is still an external-agent demonstration that inherited procedures/mechanisms cut fully loaded cost per successful task, and that deliverable is serially gated by the three blockers the prior cycle identified correctly: B1 (shipped audited parameterized carrier plus a known-negative refusal), B2 (a task bank whose cold/retrieval comparators are genuinely below ceiling), B3 (a same-model endpoint that can actually perform the minimal multi-step Web task). I therefore keep Product, Runtime and Intel dedicated to B1/B2/B3 and refuse to fund any full four-arm C-LLM-INHERIT / C-RESIDUAL-NOVELTY / C-PRODUCT-ECON execution this cycle (readiness conditions 1-3 are all still missing). The off-path lanes are re-pointed instead of left to local inertia: Graph is pivoted off its own already-parked, structurally degenerate C-FRESHNESS four-anchor route to the starved priority claim C-DELTA-REPAIR; Frontier is pivoted off a C-SEMANTIC-RESOLVE micro-benchmark that has now lost three consecutive packets to a shared control-plane defect, onto the genuinely architecture-changing acquisition-cost question; Physics keeps its orthogonal, product-relevant endpoint-barrier-stationarity question with an attainability certificate. Portfolio yield remains the dominant non-scientific cost (255/434 REVISE+MEASUREMENT_INVALID) and the same-failure counters (Product 11, Intel 11, Frontier 9) confirm that repeated control-plane design defects, not lack of activity, are the bottleneck. The freeze-time code-binding defect is real but lives in scripts/, outside every lane's allowed_code_roots, so no lane is assigned to 'repair' it; mandates are instead written to avoid re-requiring the unsatisfiable V9 literal.
director_mandate.scout_assessment: The Scout is not degraded (model_scout status=success), so its brief is staff advice cross-checked against the Codex claim state, not authority. It materially shaped this cycle in three ways. (1) I accept its central read that B1/B2/B3 form a serial gate and that Product/Runtime/Intel are each already pointed at one blocker, so all three stay CONTINUE/USE rather than being re-rotated. (2) I accept its challenge to Frontier's C-SEMANTIC-RESOLVE pivot and pivot Frontier to the acquisition-cost / site-native-discovery question; I reject its alternative orthogonal probes because structured intent canonicalization duplicates C-SEMANTIC-RESOLVE, incremental/delta propagation duplicates the C-DELTA-REPAIR work I am assigning to Graph, and compile-then-replay is close to SPIDER's own core and to the withdrawn 8.5x replay claim. (3) I partially reject its suggestion that Graph should merely honor its fail-loudly clause: the preceding accepted packet already parked the four-anchor Part II route, so I supersede the constructibility probe outright and redirect Graph to the starved C-DELTA-REPAIR claim. I also answer its open question about the shared freeze-time code-binding defect by NOT assigning any lane to repair it (scripts/ is outside every lane's allowed code roots) and by writing mandates that avoid the unsatisfiable V9 literal. Its external notes on budget-matched memory negatives, stale-memory benchmarks and strong browser-agent baselines are recorded as design priors for the eventual flagship benchmark, not as SPIDER evidence.

inherited_next_question: Under a design-contract v2 protocol (six freeze_eligibility checks: decision_rule_reachability, measurement_prerequisites, baseline_identifiability, control_sensitivity, treatment_liveness, freeze_artifacts_bound; plus independent design_review.json before freeze), can the SAME site-native-discovery acquisition question be made satisfiable and measured: on the credential-free GET-only stdlib-HTTP substrate, over a multi-host pool confirmed during DESIGN to contain DEEP (hop>=3) state items on >=2 distinct hosts/engines (>=10 total, >=3 per engine) via the frozen same-host static-<a> BFS (depth<=6, budget 250), what fraction of those DEEP items is reachable in <=K=3 fresh-agent GETs (one discovery GET + item-page GET + one spare) using ANY of the five frozen discovery channels (ROBOTS_SITEMAP, SITEMAP_XML, ON_SITE_SEARCH, RSS_ATOM, JSON_LD) - with the preregistered materiality threshold 0.50 on >=2 engines deciding whether shortest-path hop is NOT a fundamental acquisition-cost barrier (persistent path caching is not the optimization target; effort moves to discovery and substrate expansion) versus fresh deep-instance acquisition remaining path-bound with a computable persistence break-even surface - given that the v1 freeze of this exact mandate (EXP-FRONTIER-37984242167) committed an empty sampling frame (0 seeds, 0 DEEP items, 0 hosts), an absent pre-freeze control certificate, and a 0/0 primary metric unreachable in both falsifier directions, so the question remains entirely unmeasured; the explicitly recorded maintenance/invalidation alternative (re-validation GETs/bytes plus stale-replay false-accept rate vs re-derivation cost, scaling with hop and elapsed time) remains available to the Global Research Director for allocation instead.
